questions.question: Enter the average balance in your current account for the past 12 months
questions.descriptionHeader:
If you have multiple current accounts, first find the average balance for each account, then add them to get the total average.
Click the info icon given above to know how to calculate MAB.
questions.description:
What is MAB?

MAB stands for Monthly Average Balance — it’s the average amount of money you kept in your bank account during a month.

Why it matters:

Banks use this to understand how much balance you usually maintain. It helps them decide your loan eligibility or credit limit.

How to find it:

Most bank statements show your MAB directly.

If your statement doesn’t mention it, you can calculate it manually:

  1. Note your account’s closing balance on the 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th of the month.
  2. Add all those 4 amounts.
  3. Divide the total by 4 — that gives your Monthly Average Balance for that month.
  4. Repeat this for the past 12 completed months.
  5. Add all 12 months’ MAB values and divide by 12 — that gives your Average MAB (12 months).

💡 Example:
Monthly MAB values for last 12 months → ₹6,100, ₹6,400, ₹6,700, ₹6,300, ₹6,900, ₹6,500 ,₹6,400, ₹6,700, ₹6,300, ₹6,900 , ₹6,300, ₹6,900
(6100 + 6400 + 6700 + 6300 + 6900 + 6500 + ₹6,400 + ₹6,700 + ₹6,300 + ₹6,900 + + ₹6,300 + ₹6,900) ÷ 12 = ₹6,533.33 (Average MAB for last 12 months)

questions.question: Enter your average daily cash sales for the last financial year
questions.descriptionHeader: How to calculate your Average Daily Cash Sales
questions.description:
What is Average Daily Cash Sale?

Average Daily Cash Sale means the typical amount of cash your business earns per day over an entire financial year.

Why it matters:

This figure helps lenders understand your business’s daily revenue and overall financial stability. It’s an important indicator when evaluating loan eligibility.

How to calculate it:

  1. Find your total cash sales for the last financial year.
  2. Count the number of business days (or total days, if applicable) in that year.
  3. Divide total cash sales by that number of days.

💡 Example:
If your total cash sales in FY 2023–24 were ₹36,50,000, and you operated for 365 days:
₹36,50,000 ÷ 365 = ₹10,000 (Average Daily Cash Sale)

📊 Credit Score Factors

Select all factors that may have affected your CIBIL score.

⚠️ Be Honest

Banks verify your credit history. Any incorrect or inconsistent information can lead to delays or rejection of your application.

📋 Common factors affecting CIBIL
  • Delayed EMI/credit card payments
  • High credit card utilization (above 30%)
  • Multiple loan enquiries
  • Loan defaults or settlements
  • Limited credit history
💡 Good to know

Being upfront about your credit history helps our team find lenders who accept your profile and offer suitable terms.
